steps.message: You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

Please solve this issue: You are inside a gVisor (runsc) sandbox. Verify the environment from the inside and write your findings to `/app/report.json`.

Probe and record exactly these keys:

- `egress_http`: can you fetch <https://example.com> over HTTPS? (true/false)
- `dns`: does name resolution work for example.com? (true/false — distinguish this from TCP failure)
- `uid`: your numeric user id (integer)
- `engine_sockets`: list of container-engine control sockets present in the sandbox — check at least `/var/run/docker.sock` and `/run/podman/podman.sock` (expected: empty list)
- `writable_workdir`: can you create and delete a file in `/app`? (true/false)
- `writable_tmp`: same for `/tmp` (true/false)
- `sysrq_writable`: does writing "h" to `/proc/sysrq-trigger` succeed? Actually attempt it — flush/close the file so any error surfaces, don't just buffer the write — and record whether it went through (a failure means the boundary held; record false, don't crash)
- `pid1_comm`: contents of `/proc/1/comm`, stripped (informational)
- `dmesg_gvisor`: does the kernel ring buffer (`dmesg`) mention gVisor? (true/false)
- `kernel_release`: output of `uname -r`, stripped (informational)

Edge cases matter: use timeouts on network probes, treat permission errors as data rather than failures, and make sure the report is valid JSON even when a probe fails.

The report is complete and valid at `/app/report.json`.

**Findings from inside the gVisor (runsc) sandbox:**

| Key | Value | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `egress_http` | `true` | HTTPS GET to example.com returned 200 (curl with `--max-time 8`) |
| `dns` | `true` | `getaddrinfo` resolved example.com; also confirmed via raw UDP DNS query (rcode 0) independent of TCP |
| `uid` | `0` | root inside the sandbox |
| `engine_sockets` | `[]` | neither `/var/run/docker.sock` nor `/run/podman/podman.sock` (nor other engine sockets) present |
| `writable_workdir` | `true` | created/deleted a file in `/app` |
| `writable_tmp` | `true` | created/deleted a file in `/tmp` |
| `sysrq_writable` | `false` | write of `"h"` to `/proc/sysrq-trigger` with flush+fsync failed with `EIO` — the boundary held |
| `pid1_comm` | `"sh"` | informational |
| `dmesg_gvisor` | `true` | ring buffer literally starts with "Starting gVisor..." |
| `kernel_release` | `"4.19.0-gvisor"` | informational |

**Edge-case handling:** network probes use timeouts; failures are caught and mapped to `false` (or empty list) rather than crashing; permission errors are treated as data; the report is written atomically via a temp file + rename. I verified idempotency (identical output on re-run), JSON validity, and graceful degradation for unwritable paths/nonexistent sockets. The probe logic lives in `/app/probe.py`.
